decision_conditions: Reason : 1 - The proposed change of use of the outbuilding from incidental to ancillary would result in a form of development that is out of keeping with the established character of the locality. The introduction of an ancillary use in this context would fail to respect the prevailing pattern of development and the role of outbuildings within the area, leading to harm to the visual amenity of the surroundings. The scheme is therefore contrary to Policies D3 and D4 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies D12.3 and D12.4 of Merton�s Local Plan (2024).

Reason : 2 - The proposed ancillary outbuilding would contain two bedrooms and has the potential to increase noise and disruption to nearby occupants, in particular, properties at no.151&155 Dorset Road and 91&93 Daybrook Road. The proposal would therefore be contrary to, in particular, Merton's Local Plan 2024 policies D12.3 and D12.4

Reason : 3 - INFORMATIVE
Note to Applicant
In accordance with paragraph 38 of the NPPF, The London Borough of Merton  (LBM) takes a positive and proactive approach to development proposals focused on solutions. LBM works with applicants/agents in a positive and proactive manner by:
"	Offering a pre-application advice service. 
"	Where possible, suggesting solutions to secure a successful outcome.
In this instance:
"	The application was considered to be fundamentally contrary to the provisions of the Development Plan and the NPPF, and there were not considered to be any solutions to resolve this conflict. 
"	It is noted that the applicant/agent did not engage in any pre-application discussions.
"	The applicant is advised to seek pre-application advice on any resubmission.
description: APPLICATION FOR THE USE OF EXISTING OUTBUILDING AND HOME OFFICE AS ANCILLARY ACCOMMODATION
